findings.detail: The base flow was check, confirm [y/N], then download and run install.sh. The documented head flow downloads install.sh and runs it with `--plan --json-progress` as step 3, before the Confirm step. It runs under `/bin/sh` as the owner with no `--yes`. The only check before execution is a text match that the script names `--plan`. The CLI verifies nothing beyond TLS. A misissued certificate, or a compromised sandbox service, can serve a script that ignores `--plan` and acts immediately, because the script runs without any user decision. The stated guarantee that nothing is installed before `y` depends only on the untrusted script's own behavior. The documented rule 'without a terminal and without --yes, setup stops before installing' also changed from 'before downloading'. Non-interactive runs (ssh, pipes, automation) therefore now execute remote code without consent. Suggested fix: keep the explicit confirmation, or an equivalent integrity check, before executing any downloaded code. Alternatively, pin or verify the installer signature or hash before the plan run. Update TB-013/T-061 to say the consent gate no longer precedes execution.
findings.title: Downloaded installer now runs as the Mac owner before the user confirms (--plan), weakening the T-061 consent gate

findings.detail: The head docs reorder `darkbloom sandbox setup`: Download (step 2) and Plan (step 3) now come before Confirm (step 4). In the plan step the CLI executes the fetched `install.sh` with `/bin/sh` as the Mac owner (`--plan --json-progress`). It does this without `--yes` and without the owner having accepted the explanation. Per the docs, the CLI does not verify the script beyond TLS, and the script itself is what decides whether to enter plan mode: a script that merely names `--plan` qualifies. A misissued certificate or a compromised or tampered sandbox service (T-061) could therefore get code running as the owner (A-019) before any consent, including on a bare `setup`. Impact: TB-013's consent gate no longer covers first execution of the remote script. Fix: confirm before executing any downloaded content. Alternatively, pin or sign the installer and verify it in the CLI before plan mode. At minimum, update the TB-013/T-061 threat model to record that pre-confirmation execution exists and what limits it.
findings.title: Sandbox setup now runs the downloaded install.sh (plan mode) before the user confirmation step

findings.detail: The base docs said nothing is downloaded before the user answers `y`. The head docs (sandboxes.md lines 35-41) say setup first downloads the add-on's installer and asks it for its plan, running it in a no-install mode, and only then prompts. A tampered install.sh (misissued certificate, compromised sandbox service, or a hostile `--server` URL) would therefore run as the Mac owner (A-019) before any consent, instead of only after `y`. The consent gate no longer limits exposure to the installer script. Plausible trigger: the sandbox service or the network path serves a malicious install.sh, and a user who only wanted to see the plan has it executed. Fix: show a plan from locally verified data before running anything, or verify the installer's signature or pinned hash before the first execution. Failing that, document that the plan step executes downloaded code and update the TB-013/T-061 mitigations. This rests on the documented behavior only; the Swift implementation is not visible.
findings.title: Sandbox setup now downloads and runs the remote installer before the user confirms

findings.detail: SandboxInstaller.planArguments/supportsPlan (head lines 102-123) and the updated setup discussion in SandboxSetupCommand.swift say setup downloads install.sh and "asks it for the add-on's plan" before it "explains what changes and asks before installing anything". Previously the script ran only after consent. Now the remote script runs as the Mac owner before any approval. The only gate on running it is a substring check of the script's own text for "--plan", and the script is not verified at that point (the release checks happen inside the installer). A misissued certificate or compromised sandbox service could serve a script that executes its payload regardless of the flag, and the owner's confirmation no longer prevents it. Fix: run the plan step only after consent, or compute the plan from a signed or verified data source rather than by executing the downloaded script. Otherwise state in TB-013/T-061 that the script runs before consent, and keep that run sandboxed with a minimal environment.
findings.title: Downloaded installer script is now executed (--plan) before the owner approves any install

findings.detail: In the fresh-setup path, `withInstaller` downloads install.sh from the sandbox service. `sizeAndConfirm` then calls `requestAddonPlan`, which runs it with `/bin/sh <installer> --plan ...` as the Mac owner before the consent prompt (SandboxSetupCommand.swift:150-151, 220-226). Previously only static eligibility checks ran before the prompt, and the remote script ran only after the owner agreed. A misissued TLS certificate or a compromised sandbox service (T-061) can now run arbitrary code as the owner (A-019) on every `darkbloom sandbox setup`. That includes owners who would answer 'no', and the code runs before any trade-off text is shown. The `--plan` mode only limits what a well-behaved installer does; the code does not enforce it. Fix: do not run the remote script before consent. Either confirm first using the local estimate, or authenticate the installer (pinned signature or hash) before any execution. If the pre-consent run stays, update TB-013/T-061 to say that execution now precedes consent.
findings.title: Downloaded installer is now executed before the owner's confirmation

findings.detail: The head docs and Swift flow reorder `darkbloom sandbox setup` to download install.sh and run it with `/bin/sh <script> --plan --json-progress` (no `--yes`) as the Mac owner before the [y/N] confirmation (cli-reference.md steps 2-4; SandboxSetupCommand.swift requestAddonPlan). Before this PR the remote script ran only after consent. The CLI verifies the script only via TLS, and the only gate on running it is a substring check for `--plan` in the script's own text. A misissued certificate, compromised sandbox service, or hostile `--server` could serve a script that ignores `--plan` and acts immediately, so TB-013's consent gate no longer precedes first execution. 'Nothing is installed before y' now rests solely on the untrusted script's behavior. Non-interactive runs also now execute remote code before the 'stop without terminal' check. Fix: confirm before executing any downloaded script, or verify a pinned signature/hash of install.sh in the CLI before the plan run. Update TB-013/T-061 to record the pre-confirmation execution.
